subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring `agentTurn` cron jobs before they can run with an inherited model?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but any fix changes shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, persisted doctor/update behavior, and quota thresholds, so automation cannot safely choose the boundary.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin `agentTurn` jobs, make inherited model-cost exposure explicit, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow model-cost guard
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring `agentTurn` job inherits a high-cost default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split across existing RFCs
options.body: Resolve the open reason-aware backoff, budget, provenance, and schema issues separately while accepting that consent and model-inheritance policy may remain fragmented.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin `agentTurn` jobs, make inherited model-cost exposure explicit, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron, plugin scheduling, and model-selection history makes this the best available individual routing owner for a cross-surface security/product decision.
